cases.name: valid-ed25519
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ssh-ed25519 key

cases.name: valid-ecdsa-nistp256
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 key

cases.name: valid-ecdsa-nistp384
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ecdsa-sha2-nistp384 key

cases.name: valid-ecdsa-nistp521
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ecdsa-sha2-nistp521 key

cases.name: valid-rsa-2048
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ssh-rsa key

cases.name: valid-rsa-8192
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the ssh-rsa key

cases.name: valid-sk-ed25519
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com key

cases.name: valid-sk-ecdsa-nistp256
cases.note: a valid answer signed by the sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com key

cases.name: message-offer_sha256-changed
cases.note: offer_sha256 changed after signing: a genuine signature cannot carry another offer_sha256

cases.name: message-epk-changed
cases.note: epk changed after signing: a genuine signature cannot carry another epk

cases.name: message-nonce-changed
cases.note: nonce changed after signing: a genuine signature cannot carry another nonce

cases.name: message-ct-changed
cases.note: ct changed after signing: a genuine signature cannot carry another ct

cases.name: other-key
cases.note: signed by another key, which the blob names: OpenSSH accepts it without an allowed-signers file

cases.name: namespace-file
cases.note: SSHSIG namespace file

cases.name: hash-sha256
cases.note: hash_algorithm sha256: OpenSSH allows it; the guest takes sha512 only

cases.name: version-2
cases.note: SSHSIG version 2

cases.name: trailing-byte
cases.note: one byte after the SSHSIG blob

cases.name: rsa-sha2-256
cases.note: an RSA signature with SHA-256: OpenSSH accepts it; the guest takes rsa-sha2-512 only

cases.name: rsa-ssh-rsa-sha1
cases.note: an RSA signature with SHA-1 (type ssh-rsa)

cases.name: rsa-short-signature
cases.note: an RSA signature one byte shorter than the modulus: OpenSSH left-pads it; the guest refuses

cases.name: ecdsa-mpint-not-minimal
cases.note: ECDSA r with an unneeded leading zero: OpenSSH trims it; the guest refuses

cases.name: ecdsa-r-zero
cases.note: ECDSA r = 0

cases.name: ed25519-signature-63-bytes
cases.note: an Ed25519 signature one byte short

cases.name: sk-no-user-presence
cases.note: an sk-ed25519 signature with the user-present bit clear (a key made with -O no-touch-required): check-novalidate accepts it, so verify_vm.py rewrap checks the bit itself; the guest refuses

cases.name: sk-plain-signature-type
cases.note: an sk-ed25519 key with a signature of type ssh-ed25519

cases.name: answer-v1
cases.note: a v1 answer, with no signature

cases.name: sig-2401-bytes
cases.note: a sig field of 2401 bytes once decoded

cases.name: answer-4097-bytes
cases.note: an answer of 4097 bytes: the length is refused before any parse

cases.name: sig-not-canonical-base64
cases.note: a sig whose base64 has a nonzero padding bit

cases.name: epk-not-canonical-base64
cases.note: an epk whose base64 has a nonzero padding bit: it decodes to the signed bytes, and every mailbox reader refuses it before the signature

message: domain || offer_sha256 (32 raw bytes) || epk (32) || nonce (12) || ct (48)
spec: VM runtime spec r3 7.5 with the r4 erratum (AB#1022); docs/VM_GUEST.md "Re-wrap answer v2"

test_keys.note: test keys; they protect nothing. The RSA primes are kept so --check can rebuild the same bytes; the other keys come from fixed seeds in the generator.
